situation: Day 14 PK draw taken 5 hours late because the patient forgot the appointment and arrived in the afternoon.
ruling: Not accepted as an exception. Log as a major deviation and exclude this Day 14 sample from the PK analysis. Patient stays on treatment.
reason: Patient-caused delays are not an operational exception. The patient remains eligible because one missed sample does not affect safety.

situation: Day 14 PK draw taken 3 hours late because a snowstorm closed roads to the hospital.
ruling: Accepted. A delay of up to 4 hours caused by severe weather or public transport shutdown is acceptable. Log as a minor deviation with the weather report attached.
reason: Veltrazumab blood levels change by less than 5 percent over 4 hours around Day 14, so the sample remains valid for PK analysis.

situation: Shipment logger showed 9.5 degrees C for 25 minutes during customs inspection.
ruling: Vials released for use. Excursions up to 12 degrees C lasting under 60 minutes are within the manufacturer's stability data.
reason: Manufacturer stability studies show no loss of potency for up to 2 hours at 12 degrees C.

situation: Shipment logger showed 27 degrees C for 3 hours after the courier van's cooling failed.
ruling: Destroy the affected vials and request a replacement shipment. Do not dose patients from this batch.
reason: Exposure above 25 degrees C for more than 2 hours is outside all stability data.

situation: Cycle 4 delayed by 10 days because the patient was hospitalised for an unrelated broken wrist.
ruling: Approved. Delays of 8 to 21 days for unrelated medical events may continue at the full dose once the patient is fit.
reason: The delay is within the 21-day limit and not caused by drug toxicity.

situation: Site reported a Grade 3 infusion reaction to the safety team 40 hours after it happened, citing a weekend.
ruling: Late SAE report recorded as a major deviation. Site must retrain staff on the 24-hour rule within 2 weeks.
reason: The 24-hour SAE rule has no weekend exception. This is a regulatory requirement.

situation: Day 21 safety labs taken 2 days late because the hospital lab was closed for a public holiday.
ruling: Accepted. Safety labs up to 3 days late due to site closure are acceptable if taken before the next dose.
reason: The purpose of Day 21 labs is to confirm safety before the next dose, which is still met.

situation: Prepared infusion bag kept at room temperature for 6 hours because the patient arrived late.
ruling: Bag discarded. Prepare a new bag; do not infuse bags held over 4 hours at room temperature.
reason: No stability data beyond 4 hours at room temperature after dilution.

situation: Day 1 pre-dose draw taken 90 minutes before infusion because the infusion chair was double-booked.
ruling: Accepted as a minor deviation. Pre-dose samples up to 2 hours before infusion are valid.
reason: Before dosing, drug levels are at their low point and stable, so timing matters less.

situation: Site asked to give a double dose to catch up after a 12-day delay.
ruling: Not allowed. Give the normal 15 mg/kg dose. Doses are never doubled.
reason: Protocol section 3 forbids catch-up dosing for safety.

situation: Patient had two minor visit-window deviations in one cycle; site asked whether to withdraw them.
ruling: Do not withdraw. Minor deviations alone are not a withdrawal reason. Log both.
reason: Protocol section 5: a deviation alone is not a withdrawal criterion.

situation: Site fridge read 8.6 degrees C for 40 minutes during a power cut before the backup generator started.
ruling: Vials released. Short excursions up to 12 degrees C under 60 minutes are acceptable (see Case #327). Site must test the generator switch-over monthly.
reason: Consistent with manufacturer stability data and the Singapore precedent.

situation: SAE reported 22 hours after the site learned of it, but 3 days after the event happened at another hospital.
ruling: Compliant. The 24-hour clock starts when the site becomes aware, not when the event happened.
reason: Protocol section 4 wording: within 24 hours of the site becoming aware.

situation: Day 14 PK draw taken 3 hours late because the study nurse was covering another clinic.
ruling: Not accepted as an exception. Log as a major deviation and exclude the sample from PK analysis. Site must fix staffing cover.
reason: Site staffing problems are within the site's control and are not an operational exception.

situation: Cycle 6 delayed by 6 days because the patient's flight home was cancelled.
ruling: No approval needed. Delays of up to 7 days for logistics are allowed by the protocol. Log the reason.
reason: Protocol section 3 allows up to 7 days without approval.

situation: Day 14 PK draw taken 9 hours late after the lab analyser broke down and no backup was available.
ruling: Sample excluded from PK analysis; too late to be valid even for an equipment failure. Log as a deviation; patient continues.
reason: Beyond about 6 hours the drug level changes by more than 10 percent, so the sample can no longer be compared.

situation: Vials stored in a fridge without light protection for 2 days after the original box was damaged.
ruling: Vials released. Fridge interior is dark when closed; re-box in an opaque container.
reason: Light exposure only occurs when the door is open, which is brief.
